newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to waive HKEF currency futures contracts levy.
newsitem.headline: HK to waive HKEF currency futures contracts levy.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Wednesday it will waive the levy on currency futures contracts traded on the Hong Kong Futures Exchange (HKFE) to facilitate market development and help promote financial services.
All currency futures contracts traded on the Hong Kong Futures Exchange Ltd (HKFE) will be levy-free from Friday, it said in a statement.

Hong Kong's securities watchdog, the Securities and Futures Commission, currently charges a levy of US$0.13 on every US$50,000 currency futures contract traded on the HKFE, a HKFE spokesman said by telephone.
The government statement also said the levy waiver for stock options traded on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK) would be extended for another year.
The waivers follow plans to introduce legislation permitting the exchange's more flexibility in setting trading levies. -- HONG KONG NEWSROOM (852) 2843 6369
